coverage.note: This feed's first run. Five of ten items queued and all five read; four carry no street address at all — a family-film column, a school-district bond oversight lawsuit, a weekly events listing and an SFMOMA exhibition piece. They queued because the feed syndicates the whole article into <description>, so the screen matched a story shape ('school', 'museum', 'launch') in body text rather than in the headline. The screen's skips on this batch were all correct; this is the cost of its queue-on-doubt asymmetry, not a fault to fix.

findings.description: A window at the diner occupying 434 Castro Street, an official San Francisco Legacy Business trading since 1974, was broken on the evening of 20 August 2026 and cost about $3,000 to replace. The story reports it as the third window replacement in a few years, and an entrance fire around eighteen months earlier. Read and declined: see publish.note. The people named in the article — the owner, a customer, the arrested suspect — are not recorded here.

citation.label: The Voice of San Francisco, “Legacy small business, The Cove on Castro, suffers another act of vandalism,” 25 August 2026

raw.text: On Thursday, Aug. 20, shortly after closing, The Cove on Castro, an official San Francisco Legacy Business, was again vandalized.

publish.note: Fails the ten-year test in news/AGENTS.md. A window broken and replaced for $3,000 changes nothing about the building, and in ten years it tells a reader of 434 Castro Street nothing — it is not a sale, a fire, an opening, a closure, an eviction or a designation. It is also the case the module's privacy rule is built for: the story is about the owner and his family's fifty years in the business, an arrested suspect and a named customer's fundraiser, and the building is only the setting. The page is not a crime blotter. Worth noting for a future pass: that the building holds a Legacy Business is a durable fact, but this story reports it in passing rather than reporting the designation, so it is not this entry's to carry.

resolution.method: EAS exact match on 434 CASTRO ST → parcel 2647004; sf-parcels has blklot 2647004 active, 434–436 CASTRO; the 2025 roll records it as multi-family residential, built 1909. EAS puts 434, 436 CASTRO ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 434.
